claim: Jeffrey Epstein cultivated a sustained relationship with Vitaly Churkin, Russia's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, and Churkin's son Maxim, from October 2015 until Churkin's death in February 2017. Epstein's own emails and schedules, released in the DOJ Epstein files, show the contact was brokered through the Norwegian UN diplomat Terje Rod-Larsen: Churkin first came to Epstein's Manhattan home for lunch on October 25, 2015 ("Mr. Churkin came to Jeffrey's home yesterday for lunch"), after which Epstein's office sought Churkin's private phone and email. Over the next sixteen months the records document repeated lunches at Epstein's townhouse — including the October 7, 2016 lunch with Peter Thiel and a January 10, 2017 lunch with Churkin and Hyatt chairman Tom Pritzker — and a September 2016 email in which Epstein told Thiel that Churkin had been "debriefing on syria." In parallel, Epstein took on Churkin's son Maxim, who sought Epstein's "guidance going forward," sent Epstein his resume, dropped gifts at the house, and was arranged into a once-a-week role; Vitaly Churkin died in New York on February 20, 2017.

Terje Rod-Larsen later resigned the International Peace Institute presidency in 2020 over undisclosed Epstein ties/loans. Stated as documented primary fact only; no inference about the purpose of the contact is drawn. Vitaly Churkin glossed on first use.
